examples.sql: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Faculty_Participates_in"."FacID" AS e, "Faculty"."Sex" AS g, COUNT(*) AS m1 FROM "Faculty_Participates_in" JOIN "Faculty" ON "Faculty"."FacID" = "Faculty_Participates_in"."FacID"  GROUP BY "Faculty_Participates_in"."FacID", "Faculty"."Sex"), "s2" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS g, AVG("s1"."m1") AS v FROM "s1" GROUP BY "s1"."g"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS e, "s1"."g" AS g, "s1"."m1" AS m1, ("s1"."m1" - "s2"."v") AS m2 FROM "s1" JOIN "s2" ON "s1"."g" = "s2"."g" WHERE "s1"."m1" > "s2"."v"), "s4" AS (SELECT "s3"."g" AS g, SUM("s3"."m1") AS m1, AVG("s3"."m2") AS m2 FROM "s3" GROUP BY "s3"."g"), "s5" AS (SELECT AVG("s4"."m2") AS v FROM "s4"), "s6" AS (SELECT "s4"."g" AS g, "s4"."m1" AS m1, "s4"."m2" AS m2, ("s4"."m2" - "s5"."v") AS m3 FROM "s4" JOIN "s5" ON "s5"."v" IS NOT NULL WHERE "s4"."m2" > "s5"."v") SELECT SUM("s6"."m1") AS m1, AVG("s6"."m2") AS m2, AVG("s6"."m3") AS m3 FROM "s6"
examples.instruction:
Step 1. Start from each `Faculty_Participates_in` record; combine it with each `Faculty` record for which Fac ID (`Faculty.FacID`) equals Fac ID (`Faculty_Participates_in.FacID`), one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); group the kept records by Fac ID (`Faculty_Participates_in.FacID`) and faculty sex (`Faculty.Sex`); each group gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) Fac ID (`Faculty_Participates_in.FacID`); (2) faculty sex (`Faculty.Sex`); (3) the number of records in the group.
Step 2. Start from the rows of step 1; group the kept records by column (2) of step 1; each group gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) column (2) of step 1; (2) the average of column (3) of step 1 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
Step 3. Start from the rows of step 1; combine it with the rows of step 2 for which column (2) of step 1 equals column (1) of step 2 (compared as text, character by character), one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); keep only the records for which column (3) of step 1 is greater than column (2) of step 2; for each kept record, return (1) column (1) of step 1; (2) column (2) of step 1; (3) column (3) of step 1; (4) A − B. Here A is column (3) of step 1; B is column (2) of step 2.
Step 4. Start from the rows of step 3; group the kept records by column (2) of step 3; each group gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) column (2) of step 3; (2) the sum of column (3) of step 3 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none); (3) the average of column (4) of step 3 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
Step 5. Start from the rows of step 4; all kept records form one group, which gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) the average of column (3) of step 4 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
Step 6. Start from the rows of step 4; combine it with the rows of step 5 for which it is not true that column (1) of step 5 is missing, one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); keep only the records for which column (3) of step 4 is greater than column (1) of step 5; for each kept record, return (1) column (1) of step 4; (2) column (2) of step 4; (3) column (3) of step 4; (4) A − B. Here A is column (3) of step 4; B is column (1) of step 5.
Step 7 (the answer). Start from the rows of step 6; all kept records form one group, which gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) the sum of column (2) of step 6 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none); (2) the average of column (3) of step 6 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none); (3) the average of column (4) of step 6 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
